transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-15
Time: 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jenna Cho (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (DataStream Head of ML), Tom Beckett (SRE), Grace Liu (Product), Amit Sharma (Eng)

---- Auto-generated sections (partial) ----
Topics: prefix cache hit rates; KV cache tuning; prompt reuse/canonicalization; TTL and eviction; benchmark plan
Action items: see list below

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Lena Park: okay great, good morning everyone thanks for joining the weekly caching sync, quick checkin, um, Mateo and I will run through the numbers, uh Priya I think you were going to share the staging hit rates?
[00:18] Priya Nair: yeah quick note, we rolled canonicalization last tuesday on staging, um so initial numbers look promising, but there's some noise from personalization tokens so take it with a grain of salt
[00:30] Mateo Ruiz: cool, thanks. Quick context for folks — in staging we measure two layers: prefix cache (template-level reuse) and KV cache (decoder kv cache reuse across turns). Target we discussed last week was >70% combined hit rate for steady-state, right?
[00:45] Tom Beckett: that's what ops want for cost targets, yes, 70% gives us the cost profile we need for peak.
[00:52] Grace Liu: and product wants the UX to remain sub-100ms p50 for short prompts, just so we keep the latency story.
[01:05] Mateo Ruiz: right, so quick numbers: baseline (before canonicalization) — prefix cache hit ~28%, KV cache hit ~37%, combined effective hit ~33%. After prompt canonicalization on staging: prefix ~52%, KV ~44%, combined ~48%. So that's ~15pp improvement on prefix but still shy of 70.
[01:35] Priya Nair: yeah those match what I saw. We also filtered out requests with heavy personalization (user-specific IDs), and if we exclude those, prefix hit climbs to 61% but they represent about 12% of traffic.
[01:50] Lena Park: ok that's useful, so main leakage is personalization and subtle template variations — different punctuation, whitespace, session tokens embedded.
[02:04] Amit Sharma: right, our frontend sometimes injects convo metadata inline which is bad for cache keys, I can make a change to strip that.
[02:12] Tom Beckett: just to flag — when we changed batching patterns last week we saw a small regression in KV hit rates, maybe due to micro-batching mixing sequence lengths?
[02:23] Mateo Ruiz: yep that can happen. If batch composition mixes sequences with very different prefix lengths the KV cache effectiveness drops for the shorter ones. We recommended batch by shape in the doc.
[02:35] Jenna Cho: action note: we should confirm batching policy in staging matches the recommended batch-by-shape.
[02:42] [crosstalk] Priya: ok i'll check that

[03:10] Mateo Ruiz: moving to canonicalization details — we hashed the normalized prompt (lowercase, trim whitespace, remove session ids, replace user placeholders with tokens) and used that as the prefix cache key, additionally we added a small canonicalization map for common misspellings/nlp variations. Implementation is in the patch linked in the deck.
[03:35] Priya Nair: curious — does the canonicalization preserve critical-phrases for downstream scoring? we had one false positive where a de-dup step removed 'not' around sentiment clauses and that changed model output.
[03:48] Mateo Ruiz: good catch — we explicitly exclude semantic-critical tokens from general replacements. The rule engine keeps a whitelist of tokens never to touch; 'not' would be on that list. That said, you found a gap, send example and we'll update rules.
[03:58] Amit Sharma: i'll paste the example in slack after the call.

[04:25] Grace Liu: on TTL — what are we using now? I saw 5 minutes for prefix keys and 30 minutes for KV entries in staging.
[04:32] Mateo Ruiz: staging default TTLs are conservative: prefix 5m, KV 30m. For production we suggested 10m prefix / 60m KV for workloads with moderate reuse. But depends on memory pressure and eviction policy.
[04:45] Tom Beckett: production memory pressure is real — we have GPUs with limited cache memory, eviction must be LRU-ish. Can we measure miss cost? i.e., tokens and latency delta when we miss vs hit.
[04:56] Mateo Ruiz: yes we have a benchmark spreadsheet. Miss => average +85ms token latency and about 1.2x GPU cycles per request (varies by seq len). We'll share the sheet.

[05:20] Priya Nair: question about partial hits — if prefix matches but KV doesn't, what's effective behavior?
[05:27] Mateo Ruiz: if prefix hits but kv miss then we still save tokenization + first-pass decoding ops, so latency improves but not as much as full KV hit. In our numbers partial hits gave ~40% of full-hit benefit.
[05:40] Lena Park: ok, product question — should we push more canonicalization to the client to maximize prefix reuse, or centralize on our side? Tradeoffs?
[05:50] Grace Liu: i prefer client-side canonicalization to reduce network churn, but it's more rollout complexity.
[06:00] Priya Nair: we can't change all clients quickly; better to do server-side now and then optionally push client helpers.

[06:20] Tom Beckett: SRE note — any change that canonicalizes must be idempotent and reversible for debugging. When we hash keys we need a way to map back to raw prompt for audits.
[06:31] Mateo Ruiz: agreed — we log canonicalization diffs (hashed) and keep a short retention of raw inputs for 7 days in staging logs (encrypted), in prod we can integrate with KMS and audit logs as needed.

[07:00] Priya Nair: on the subject of hit-rate targets, is 70% realistic for our mix? we have many short templated prompts but also quite a bit of personalization.
[07:10] Lena Park: based on similar customers we see 65-75% for templated-heavy apps after canonicalization + client fixes. With 12% heavy personalization edge, realistic near-term target is 60-68%.

[07:35] Amit Sharma: we can work on reducing personalization in prompt bodies; some of it is only needed in metadata. we'll try to lift it out of the prompt.

[08:00] Mateo Ruiz: quick demo snapshot — show staging dashboard numbers (spoken): 7:00-8:30 window — 250k requests, prefix hits 52%, KV hits 44%, combined 48%, tail latency p95 320ms, p50 95ms.
[08:25] Priya Nair: tail latency spikes align with big sequences from onboarding flows.
[08:33] Mateo Ruiz: yes, onboarding flows include long context, which reduces batching efficiency and KV reuse. Two levers: pre-warm with warm tokens or isolate onboarding to its own smaller pool with tuned model variant.

[09:00] Grace Liu: product asks — what's the UX impact if we isolate onboarding to a different pool? Additional cost?
[09:07] Lena Park: small cost bump but better SLAs for onboarding. We can simulate cost delta in the spreadsheet.

[09:30] Tom Beckett: question about cache key collisions — are we using a strong hash (sha256) or something shorter? we hit one collision during a stress test last month.
[09:40] Mateo Ruiz: we use sha256 truncated to 64 hex chars; collision probability negligible. We think the stress collision was a bug in the shuffle when keys were persisted; SE will check log correlation.

[10:02] Priya Nair: got it. Another item — we saw KV eviction churn causing low effective KV hits during peak bursts. Is there a recommended eviction policy change?
[10:12] Mateo Ruiz: for bursty workloads we recommend a two-tier cache: sticky for hot prefixes (higher TTL) and LRU for the rest. Hotness is measured by recent frequency. We'll propose parameters after we see your heatmap.

[10:30] Amit Sharma: how do we identify 'hot' prefixes without too much overhead?
[10:35] Mateo Ruiz: approximate counting (count-min sketch) or lightweight sampling; you can run a daily job to mark top N prefixes. We'll include sample config.

[11:00] Lena Park: ok let's talk about next week's benchmark plan — Priya, you will run 24h production-shaped traffic against staging with canonicalization and client-side stripping for a subset. We want before/after hit rates and tail latency.
[11:16] Priya Nair: yes that's doable; i'll run it starting monday and share logs.

[11:30] Grace Liu: we also wanted to explore lowering prefix TTL slightly to reduce stale noise — maybe 8 minutes instead of 10, while increasing KV TTL to 90 minutes? Thoughts?
[11:40] Mateo Ruiz: lowering prefix TTL reduces memory footprint but can slightly lower prefix hit. If KV TTL is long, some misses will still recover on KV. We'll test 8/90 in staging.

[12:05] Tom Beckett: ops needs an alert if effective combined hit rate dips below 45% for longer than 10 minutes during business hours. Can Redwood create that dashboard alert?
[12:14] Lena Park: yes we can add alert and tie to Ops slack channel.

[12:30] Priya Nair: tiny nit — we saw a handful of cases where prompt canonicalization changed capitalization-sensitive product codes; need to ensure code tokens are preserved. I'll annotate the list.
[12:40] Mateo Ruiz: please send the list, we'll update the whitelist rules.

[13:05] Jenna Cho: recapping next steps internally: Mateo will push canonicalization patch to staging, Lena will send tuning doc, Priya will run the 24h benchmark, Tom will upload SRE logs, Amit will strip inline metadata in frontend for the sample clients.

[13:30] Grace Liu: timeline — aim to reconvene the week of 4/21 for TTL/eviction policy deep dive.

[13:45] Priya Nair: sounds good, thanks everyone.

[14:00] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll share the links (benchmark sheet, patch link, tuning doc) in the follow-up email. Bye.
